topics.topic: Boundary between runtime_settings normalization and configuration presence and validity checks
questions: Does per-item normalization merely preserve parse results for `configuration`, or may `runtime_settings` reject malformed values even though `configuration` owns the ordered well-formedness checks and first diagnostic?

Does `runtime_settings` enforce absence by emitting a missing value, or does `configuration` own the entire no-default decision and reject absence? The `configuration` section also claims “that no default is applied (rule 5)”.
Which module decides that one individual item is malformed, given that `runtime_settings` hides per-item normalization while `configuration` owns the ordered check that each item is well formed?

Which module decides that an individual environment item is missing or malformed: `runtime_settings`, which assigns types and performs per-item normalization, or `configuration`, which owns the ordered presence and well-formedness checks?

quotes:
A17 rules 1 and 5 for each item alone: a required item missing or
malformed refused, naming the item and never its value; no default applied.
The checks across items are `configuration.load_configuration`'s.
judgement.why: State 5 assigns per-item missing, malformed and no-default enforcement to `runtime_settings`, while `configuration` owns checks across items.

topics.topic: Environment-setting names and ownership of the environment schema
questions: Does `runtime_settings` own the exact environment-variable names as part of its closed table, or does `data_provider` own and export them?
Which module owns the exact environment-variable-name table, and what are the exact names for the store path, backup path, backup key, owner credential and four service tokens?

What is the exact environment-variable name, field name, type and normalization rule for each item, and which module owns those names, given that `runtime_settings` knows only `models` while the text also says the variables' names belong to the data closure?

quotes:
A17 rule 1's reading of the environment, and only it: the closed table of
the `REGISTRY_` items — the store's location, the backup location, the
backup key, the owner credential, the four service tokens — loaded at each
call of `load_runtime_settings` into the settings, each item with its type,
whether it is required (the four tokens each optional, every other item
required) and its normalization; no default for any item (A17 rule 5); a
variable that names no item is not read (owner, 2026-11-11). Emitted
deterministically (SPEC_STANDARD §6.11); the variables' names are the data
closure's.

The typed constants of the data closure, the one home of each value the
generated code reads that is not a setting of the environment (SPEC_STANDARD
§6.10, §15.3.1; reopened 2026-11-11, replacing the former
release_declarations module)
judgement.divergence: One implementation makes the exact environment-variable names part of `runtime_settings`' closed table, while another imports them from `data_provider`; the owner notices because the same supplied variable starts Registry in one implementation and is treated as a missing setting in the other.
judgement.why: The text assigns the closed environment table to `runtime_settings` but says its variable names belong to the data closure without identifying their single owning module or listing the names.

witness.initial: Registry has an otherwise complete environment and no existing store at the configured location.
events: The owner sets `REGISTRY_STORE_PATH` to the intended store path.
outcomes: An implementation whose `runtime_settings` table names `REGISTRY_STORE_PATH` loads the setting and continues startup.
An implementation whose data-closure table names the item differently does not read `REGISTRY_STORE_PATH` and stops with the store location missing.
basis:
Only `runtime_settings` reads the process
environment, and only the `REGISTRY_` items A17 rule 1 lists (owner,
2026-11-11); every other module receives the settings it needs from
`configuration`, which checks them.

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2)

topics.topic: Module responsible for creating the initial M12 AuditSequence record
questions: Which module creates the initial AuditSequence row at 0, given that `audit_log` owns M12 but `store` creates the new database and may not know the later `audit_log` module?

Which module creates and persists the initial M12 record in the transaction that creates a store, given that `audit_log` owns M12 but `store` is earlier in the dependency order and may not know `audit_log`?

Who creates the initial M12 record in a new store? `audit_log` owns M12 but is later than `store` and cannot be known by it; `store` owns making the new store but must not own which domain record is written; and `instance_lifecycle` does not list `audit_log` among the modules it knows.

quotes:
A14 and A15: appending an entry (M09) inside the transaction of the change it
records, with the next sequence number after the last the store's history ever
wrote, kept apart from the entries — M12 AuditSequence, made at 0 with a new
store — so an erasure never lowers it (A15 rule 5);

Which record a module writes or when; any domain check; the audit log's
sequence rule (A15 rule 5 is `audit_log`'s, which keeps its counter through
`store`); encrypting or keeping a backup (`backups`).

A module may know only modules on earlier lines of the list, never one on a
later line, and modules on one line do not know each other.
judgement.divergence: One implementation has `store` create the `audit_log`-owned M12 record atomically while making the database, while another creates an empty database and relies on a later initialization step; the owner notices an interrupted store that either opens with sequence 0 or lacks the required sequence and fails or is repaired.
judgement.why: M12 must exist at zero with a new store, but no permitted dependency or owner is assigned responsibility for creating it during `store`'s new-store operation.

The database was created without M12 because `store` may not own the audit record; restart must reject or repair it, or the first audit append must invent initialization behavior.

that name and no other file (A17 rule 5), and removing a store it made new
when the start then fails at a listener (A17 rule 2);

For every other change, `operations` opens
the transaction through `store.run_in_transaction`,
calls each module the action
changes inside it, appends the action's one audit entry through
`audit_log.append_audit_entry` when the action changed state and M09 lists
it (A14 rule 1)
and commits once.

topics.topic: Scope of data_provider ownership versus model-owned enumerations and other values
questions: Are enumeration members and numeric form bounds values owned by `data_provider`, or are model enumerations and structural bounds exceptions to this assertion?
Are the member values of the non-artifact enumerations owned by `models` or constants owned by `data_provider`, and which module changes when an enumeration member changes?

Does `data_provider` own only release policy constants, or literally every non-environment value read by generated code, including stored model facts, request values, clock readings and transaction results that other modules own?

quotes:
The typed constants of the data closure, the one home of each value the
generated code reads that is not a setting of the environment (SPEC_STANDARD
§6.10, §15.3.1; reopened 2026-11-11, replacing the former
release_declarations module)

The models M01–M12 as the domain's vocabulary, the declared vocabularies of
State 1 as enumerations — for the artifact types only the shape of a type
with its owner service, whose rows are `data_provider`'s, so a stored
pointer of a type a later release removed still reads (A22 rule 4) — and the disclosure class
of every fact ("Disclosure classes by field"),
the order of the classes (A09 rule 4), and the refusal vocabulary: each refusal
kind with the stage of A04 rule 6 it belongs to.

judgement.why: The universal data-provider ownership claim includes enumeration values that the `models` section explicitly owns, with only artifact-type rows stated as the exception.

topics.topic: Whether and why backups directly depends on audit_log
questions: What symbol does `backups` directly use from `audit_log`, given that `store.copy_store_snapshot` must return the audit sequence read as the snapshot's first read?
Why may `backups` know `audit_log` when `store.copy_store_snapshot` is specified to return the snapshot's sequence and the `store` section says the reading needs no upward call to `audit_log`?

What does `backups` directly import or call from `audit_log`? The store section says `copy_store_snapshot` reads M12 as the snapshot's first read and returns that exact sequence without an upward call, so using `audit_log.last_audit_sequence` would be redundant and could race the snapshot.

judgement.why: The declared `backups` dependency on `audit_log` has no directly used symbol because `store.copy_store_snapshot` supplies the snapshot sequence and the text expressly says no upward audit-log call is needed.
judgement.rule:
Если consumer не импортирует ни одного символа provider-а, ребро provider-а
  отсутствует целиком.

What are the exact `RELEASE_VERSION` and `CONTRACT_VERSION` values, and are they literals in `data_provider` or injected deterministically by the release build?
What exact host/interface and port are `OWNER_INTERFACE_LISTEN_ADDRESS` and `SERVICE_API_LISTEN_ADDRESS`?
What exact value does `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` have: 60 seconds or some other interval no greater than one minute?

topics.topic: Module responsible for enforcing import upload size before accepting the body
questions: Which module reads the request stream and refuses it before parsing or replacing the session's kept file: `owner_interface`, `operations`, `migration_import`, or `owner_sessions`?

Which module reads the request's declared length and limits the body before bytes are received? `migration_import` owns the size check and knows `data_provider`, but `owner_interface` owns the HTTP upload boundary, does not know either module, and says it owns no server check.

judgement.why: The `migration_import` ownership section assigns reading the uploaded file, applying the release size limit and refusing an unreadable upload to `migration_import`.

topics.topic: Normalization and byte representation of secret settings and presented credentials
questions: What is each setting's concrete type and normalization, especially the text-to-bytes encoding for secrets and whether whitespace or Unicode normalization is applied?

In what byte representation are environment-provided credentials measured and compared, and how are browser or header text values decoded to those bytes before the 32-byte check and constant-time comparison?

quotes:
A17 rule 1's reading of the environment, and only it: the closed table of
the `REGISTRY_` items — the store's location, the backup location, the
backup key, the owner credential, the four service tokens — loaded at each
call of `load_runtime_settings` into the settings, each item with its type,
whether it is required (the four tokens each optional, every other item
required) and its normalization; no default for any item (A17 rule 5);

A17: the start checks of rule 2 in its one order over the settings
`runtime_settings` loads — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value;

Minting every opaque identity of a record or an action — `project_id`,
`room_id`, pointer id, `customer_ref`, the confirmation id — as a random UUID
("Identity formats"); making the values of A13 rule 7 — the owner session's
identity, its CSRF value, a confirmation value — of at least 32 bytes from the
operating system's random source; comparing a presented secret with a
held one in constant time (A13 rule 7, A17 rule 6).
judgement.divergence: One implementation preserves a non-ASCII credential exactly and measures its UTF-8 bytes, while another trims, normalizes or counts characters; the owner observes a different startup decision or a credential that authenticates differently.
judgement.why: The text says each environment item has a normalization and that secrets are measured as bytes but never defines the secret representation or normalization.

witness.initial: The configured owner credential contains non-ASCII characters and leading or trailing spaces, with fewer than 32 code points but at least 32 UTF-8 bytes.
events: The owner later presents the same visible credential at sign-in.
outcomes: Exact preservation with UTF-8 byte counting accepts the configuration and authenticates the exact value.
Trimming, Unicode normalization or character counting rejects startup or authenticates a different normalized value.
witness.observer: The owner at startup or sign-in
basis:
`configuration` holds the secrets and hands each only to the module that
uses it: the service tokens to `service_access`, the owner credential to
`owner_sessions`, the backup key to `backups`.

topics.topic: How configuration performs constant-time secret comparison through random_values

quotes:
every comparison of a presented secret with a held one goes
through `random_values.equal_in_constant_time` (A13 rule 7, A17 rule 6).

A17: the start checks of rule 2 in its one order over the settings
`runtime_settings` loads — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value;
judgement.why: The constant-time rule is expressly limited to comparing a presented secret with a held secret; configuration distinctness compares two loaded settings, so it does not require a dependency on `random_values`.
